judged_text: remove_member silently no-ops (and returns success) when user_id is not a member of the group, and group.save on an untouched record can never fail so the 422 branch is dead. A stale UI or double-invocation sends a user_id that was already removed; the endpoint returns success, the client reloads and shows the member still present or the removal 'succeed' with nothing done — no error distinguishes a real removal from a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. There is no check that the user was actually a member (so deleting a non-member is a no-op but still returns success), and `group.save` is unlikely to fail here since the association deletion happens immediately and the `group` record itself is typically unchanged/valid, making the 422 branch effectively unreachable. However, this is more about endpoint semantics/idempotency and dead error-handling than a clearly broken behavior from the diff (the client also reloads members on success).
